notable_absence.finding: Purely a three-item navigational hub page (Capella UI / SDK / CLI tools), each pointing to a single child page - no independent technical content, no privileges, roles, editions, or version citations. Neither of the batch's two known recurring anomalies appears.

cross_component_finding: Registry naming inconsistency recurrence: cbimport/cbexport were minted as server:cbimport/server:cbexport in cloud/connect/cli-import-export.json but as tool:cbimport/tool:cbexport in cloud/reference/command-line-tools.json - two different namespace prefixes for the same real-world tool, discovered while resolving this page's two separate links to those pages. Flagging for coordinator reconciliation, not resolving here. Separately, this page is the load-bearing confirmation that the three bulk-load paths identified separately across rounds 6/7/8 (capella:data-api's HTTP passthrough is notably NOT one of the three listed here, capella:import-tool's browser UI, sdk:bulk-import-workflow's SDK scripting, and server:cbimport/cbexport's CLI tools) are understood by Couchbase's own docs structure as the complete set of three import/export mechanisms - the guide's own taxonomy (UI / SDK / CLI) omits the Data API entirely as an import path, which is useful negative evidence: bulk document loading is not one of the Data API's documented use cases in this docs tree, contrasting with capella:data-api's Query/Search passthrough scope established in round 6.
cross_product_finding: Confirms the round-brief's specific question: import.md and load.md do not reveal anything conceptually new about bulk data loading beyond capella:data-api (round 6) or capella:import-tool (round 7) as standalone mechanisms - rather, load.md is the hub page that organizes those two mechanisms (retroactively confirming capella:import-tool was correctly identified in round 7) plus a third mechanism (server:cbimport/cbexport CLI tools, already minted in round 8's cloud/connect/cli-import-export.json) plus a fourth (sdk:bulk-import-workflow, newly minted in this batch's import.json). No fifth or hidden mechanism was found.
